absent: Bodies of logic port accessors and registration plus lookup of port ranges.
Numeric value of IO space limit and global allocation policy.
Lifecycle operations for the recency cache beyond lock helpers, including creation, lookup, insertion, eviction and commit.
Concrete hook signatures enumerated in hook definition headers.
Static call patching mechanics and activation control.
Internal dequeue routine selecting between ready staging and producer head.
Compression and decompression algorithms, streaming transitions and failure handling beyond result codes.

findings.text: Descriptor logic_pio_hwaddr chains through a list link, records firmware identity, opaque host context with an operation table, hardware and logical base addresses, extent size and mode flags. Operation table offers scalar input with scalar output plus block input with block output, each parameterized by transfer width and element count. Mode enumeration separates indirect window handling from direct CPU mapped handling.

Generic port accessor names for byte, word and long widths plus repeating block input and output forms are redirected to logic layer implementations, funneling all port traffic through indirect or mapped handlers.
Indirect window extent equals 0x4000 when enabled and 0 when indirect support is disabled. Upper mapped bound equals IO space limit reduced by the current indirect extent.
Each header in this lane defines a single include guard that makes repeated inclusion idempotent. Guard presence carries no behavioral contract beyond preventing double definition.

Element wrapper lc_element tracks hash collision linkage, membership in active or free ordering, outstanding reference count, stable slot index, current label with free sentinel and pending replacement label. Cache object lru_cache maintains recency, free, in-use and pending-change orderings, backing slab cache, element sizing with member offset, capacity with pending limits and counters, usage statistics, flag word, descriptive name, hash buckets and indexed element table.
Free marker equals all bits set in an unsigned value. Maximum active population equals two raised to the twenty fourth power, bounding slot indices so high bits stay available for future flags.

Four single-bit flags record debugging paranoia for detecting concurrent access, dirty accumulation across a transaction, locked exclusion blocking further changes and serializing commits, and starvation when neither free nor reclaimable slots remain. Each mask occupies one distinct bit position.

Transaction admission uses atomic test and set on the locked bit and succeeds only when previously clear. Release clears the dirty indication before releasing locked with ordering that publishes prior updates. Callers must externally serialize mutation; the paranoia bit only helps detect violations.
Helper lc_entry recovers an enclosing tracked object from a member pointer when given the containing type and member name.

Each security module exposes a tiny property carrier holding its native credential reference when its configuration is enabled and holding nothing otherwise. AppArmor keeps a label pointer, SELinux and BPF keep numeric security identifiers, and Smack keeps a known-label pointer. The empty variant preserves layout compatibility.

Network audit carrier records interface index, socket reference, address family, destination and source ports, plus a family-selected address pair for either IPv4 or IPv6 endpoints. Companion carriers record ioctl path with command, InfiniBand subnet prefix with partition key, and device name with port number.

Common audit envelope carries a small discriminant selecting one active payload among filesystem, network, capability, IPC, task, key, module, inode, dentry, ioctl, file, InfiniBand, lockdown, notification, anonymous inode and netlink message forms, alongside a second module-specific pointer chosen among Smack, SELinux and AppArmor private data.

Discriminant values are path one, net two, capability three, IPC four, task five, key six, none seven, module eight, inode nine, dentry ten, ioctl eleven, file twelve, partition key thirteen, end port fourteen, lockdown fifteen, notification sixteen, anonymous inode seventeen and netlink type eighteen. Two short aliases expose the version-specific address pairs inside the network family union.

Two inline audit helpers accept an envelope with callback pointers but perform no work in the presented configuration, representing a disabled-logging fallback where callers remain valid yet emit nothing.

Each optional security or integrity subsystem contributes a counting token that yields a single list element when its configuration is active and vanishes otherwise, allowing a uniform variadic count across fourteen independent options.
Total module capacity is derived by counting surviving tokens through a two-stage variadic helper, with a fallback definition of zero when counting support is unavailable.

Hook dispatch combines a per-hook function pointer union with a generic address slot, a static call site bundling key, trampoline, hook list and activation flag, a packed table replicating call sites per hook up to module capacity, an identity pairing name with numeric identifier, and a list node binding a call site array to one union member and one identity.

Size table holds unsigned byte counts for per-object security storage across credentials, tasks, files, backing files, inodes, superblocks, IPC, sockets, InfiniBand, keys, messages, perf events, extended attribute slots, tunnel devices, block devices and BPF map, program and token objects.

Void hook result expands to a null statement. Legacy-major occupies bit zero and exclusive occupies bit one. Ordering places capabilities at negative one, mutable modules at zero and integrity at positive one.

Hook initializer binds a named table slot to a concrete function. Module descriptor records identity, ordering, flag word, blob size table, enable switch, general init entry and a chain of callbacks spanning pure, early, core, subsystem, filesystem, device, late and late-synchronized phases. Two placement helpers emit descriptors into regular and early init sections with pointer alignment.
Extended attribute slot allocator returns null when no array is supplied and otherwise hands out the next indexed slot while advancing the shared count.
Light queue node wraps a lockless list link. Queue object combines a spin lock, a singly linked ready chain consumed under that lock, and a lockless head receiving concurrent producers.

Initialization prepares the spin lock, empties ready staging and prepares the producer head. Emptiness holds only when both staging and producer sides show no entries, observed with acquire ordering. Single and batch producers append to the lockless side and report whether staging appeared empty, with batch input normalized to arrival order before insertion.

Dequeue helper extracts at most one staged node and converts it to a typed container or yields null when empty. Iteration helper walks a mutable singly linked result while tolerating removal of the current element.

Memory usage level is fourteen. Hash logarithm equals usage less two, with table entry counts equal to one shifted by usage and by that logarithm. Largest accepted input is 0x7E000000 bytes. Worst-case expansion adds a fractional share plus sixteen bytes and signals zero on oversize. Default acceleration is one. High-compression levels span three through sixteen with nine as default. Dictionary logarithm is sixteen with maximum distance one shifted by it, associated masks subtracting one, and hash sizing one logarithm lower.

Forward stream occupies one shifted by usage less three plus four address units, scaled by eight bytes per unit. High-compression stream occupies 262192 bytes with a size-t count variant dividing by element size. Decode stream occupies four address units scaled similarly.

Each codec state pairs an opaque fixed-size table with a structured view. Fast stream view keeps hash table, current offset, initialization marker, dictionary pointer, output start and retained size. High-compression view keeps hash and chain tables, prefix end, base and dictionary base pointers, dictionary and low limits, update cursor and level. Decode view keeps external dictionary pointer with size plus prefix end with size.

Memory aliases equate single-shot workspace with corresponding stream extents. Bound wrapper forwards size to the expansion rule. In-place decoding margin equals input shifted right by eight plus thirty two. Maximum match distance defaults to 65535.
Single-method workspace equals 8192 short units, reused as general workspace size. Worst-case expansion equals input plus its sixteenth plus sixty nine bytes of fixed overhead.

Result codes use zero for success and negative one through negative ten for distinct failures covering generic error, memory exhaustion, incompressible input, input overrun, output overrun, lookbehind overrun, missing end marker, unconsumed input, unimplemented path and invalid argument.
Cache entry chains on a global list, participates in a hashed bucket through lockless-aware linkage, carries an atomic reference count, stable hash key, flag word and opaque sixty four bit value.

List membership is guarded by the cache list lock while hash linkage is guarded by per-bucket chain locking. Positive reference count pins the entry hashed; reaching zero permits unhashing and reclamation, and deletion attempts fail while references remain. Key and value stay immutable across lifetime.

Transaction lifecycle accumulates index to label moves on a pending queue up to a configured ceiling, then serializes commit under the locked bit with dirty marking, publishes changes and releases both marks. Absence of free and unused slots enters starvation, withholding new references until some count drops to zero.
Concurrent mutation without external exclusion risks list and hash corruption despite a debug flag. Undersized capacity manifests as frequent starvation and stalled progress.
Dropping the final reference triggers unhash and free, so use after release or deletion without holding a reference risks use-after-free or silent failure.
Oversize inputs yield a zero bound rather than a usable size. Callers that ignore this sentinel risk undersized allocation and overrun.
